problem_text:
A logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over a 17-day operational window.  
The starting stock at the outset of this period is 33 gallons.  
In each day \( t = 1, \dots, 17 \), the supplier permits the company to submit a purchase request, the volume of which must fall between 17 and 65 gallons.  
Nevertheless, every order placed will experience a delivery lag of 3 days before it becomes available to meet consumption needs or to rebuild stock levels.  
The daily consumption of the additive is provided as follows:  

* Day 1: 18 gallons  
* Day 2: 30 gallons  
* Day 3: 52 gallons  
* Day 4: 57 gallons  
* Day 5: 27 gallons  
* Day 6: 41 gallons  
* Day 7: 40 gallons  
* Day 8: 48 gallons  
* Day 9: 31 gallons  
* Day 10: 27 gallons  
* Day 11: 51 gallons  
* Day 12: 14 gallons  
* Day 13: 39 gallons  
* Day 14: 58 gallons  
* Day 15: 20 gallons  
* Day 16: 16 gallons  
* Day 17: 42 gallons  

Stockouts are tolerated, but any unsatisfied consumption is considered lost and will not be deferred to later days.  
Throughout the 17-day horizon, additive quantities may be treated as continuous values, and the total volume of fuel additive physically present in the storage tank at any moment must remain below the capacity limit of 48 gallons.  
The aggregate expenditure over the planning interval comprises three elements: the procurement expense, amounting to 5 per gallon ordered; the storage expense, calculated as 2 per gallon retained overnight; and the penalty for unmet consumption, assessed at 12 per gallon short.  
The objective is to establish the optimal purchase volume for each day and to monitor the ensuing stock and deficit quantities so as to minimize the total cost.
